rapport_notes: Rep builds genuine warmth through active listening to customer's personal struggles and mirrors back empathy; tone is warm and conversational throughout.

evidence_quotes.quid_pro_quo: None — rep launches directly into logistics probing ('what kind of packing services were you needing') with no time-boxed framing or promise of an accurate quote.
evidence_quotes.their_agenda: Never asked. Rep goes straight to packing type and square footage without asking 'Other than price, what are your biggest concerns about this move?'
evidence_quotes.two_layers_deep: N/A — no agenda established, so no concerns to probe. However, when customer raises concern about six-to-seven-hour estimate seeming too long, rep responds with explanation but does not ask 'tell me more' or 'what else concerns you' — one-layer response only.
evidence_quotes.sheet1_careful_with: Mentioned in opening bundle: 'damage coverage that covers up to $2,000 worth of damage' — answered in Stage 1 as part of initial rate explanation, not raised by customer concern.
evidence_quotes.sheet2_whos_coming: Never mentioned. No 'Meet Your Mover' or 'who's actually showing up' language anywhere in the call.
evidence_quotes.on_time_guarantee: Covered in Stage 1 opening: 'if we don't arrive in the window that we say we're gonna be there, then money is automatically taken off of your final checkout.'
evidence_quotes.communication: Never mentioned. No day-before call, named crew lead, or inbox updates discussed.
evidence_quotes.estimate_anchor: Partial anchor given: 'typically for a unit this size like a one bedroom apartment generally it takes about three to three and a half' hours for packing, but no personalization to customer's specific situation (light furniture load) until after estimate is stated. Customer explicitly raises that she doesn't have much stuff; rep acknowledges but does not re-anchor down from the 6–7 hour range.
evidence_quotes.estimate_window: Rep states: 'this would be simply just an estimate that I'm giving you based off of just the general information that I have' and 'you only pay for the time you use so we have a minimum of two and a half hours... if they get there and it's not as much stuff as you know we're estimating... then that's all you're gonna be paying for.'
evidence_quotes.beats_it_pay_less: Covered: 'if you only end up using the truck for five hours and that's all you pay for' / 'if the crew beats it, you pay less' concept is present.
evidence_quotes.self_prep_tip: Never mentioned. No guidance on what customer can pre-pack to reduce bill.
evidence_quotes.close: No rate-lock statement. No explicit ask like 'would you like our help with your move?' — customer initiates close by saying 'I would love to go ahead and book me.' Rep confirms 'I got you reserved' but did not ask; customer volunteered.

top_strength: Rep demonstrates exceptional emotional intelligence and rapport-building by genuinely listening to the customer's life circumstances (family blessings, fatigue, promotion) and validating her need for help, which directly led to the booking.
coaching_note: Skip the logistics dump entirely and lead with 'Other than price, what are your biggest concerns about this move?' before asking any questions—this is the highest-leverage moment to uncover what matters to the customer and avoids the 'asked but did nothing with it' trap.
